Now, it is proposed to enact a new law, namely, the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita Bill, 2023 by 
repealing the Indian Penal Code to streamline provisions relating to offences and penalties. It is proposed 
to provide first time community service as one of the punishments for petty offences. The offences 
against women and children, murder and offences against the State have been given precedence. The 
various offences have been made gender neutral. In order to deal effectively with the problem of 
organised crimes and terrorist activities, new offences of terrorist acts and organised crime have been 
added in the Bill with deterrent punishments. A new offence on acts of secession, armed rebellion, 
subversive activities, separatist activities or endangering sovereignty or unity and integrity of India has 
also been added. The fines and punishment for various offences have also been suitably enhanced.

Robbery.—(1) In all robbery there is either theft or extortion. 
(2) Theft is robbery if, in order to the committing of the theft, or in committing the theft, or in 
carrying away or attempting to carry away property obtained by the theft, the offender, for that end 
voluntarily causes or attempts to cause to any person death or hurt or wrongful restraint, or fear of instant 
death or of instant hurt, or of instant wrongful restraint. 
(3) Extortion is robbery if the offender, at the time of committing the extortion, is in the presence of 
the person put in fear, and commits the extortion by putting that person in fear of instant death, of instant 
hurt, or of instant wrongful restraint to that person or to some other person, and, by so putting in fear, 
induces the person so put in fear then and there to deliver up the thing extorted. 
Explanation.—The offender is said to be present if he is sufficiently near to put the other person in 
fear of instant death, of instant hurt, or of instant wrongful restraint. 
(a) A holds Z down, and fraudulently takes Z’s money and jewels from Z’s clothes, without Z’s 
consent. Here A has committed theft, and, in order to the committing of that theft, has voluntarily caused 
wrongful restraint to Z. A has therefore committed robbery. 
(b) A meets Z on the high road, shows a pistol, and demands Z’s purse. Z, in consequence, surrenders 
his purse. Here A has extorted the purse from Z by putting him in fear of instant hurt, and being at the 
time of committing the extortion in his presence. A has therefore committed robbery. 
(c) A meets Z and Z’s child on the high road. A takes the child, and threatens to fling it down a 
precipice, unless Z delivers his purse. Z, in consequence, delivers his purse. Here A has extorted the 
purse from Z, by causing Z to be in fear of instant hurt to the child who is there present. A has therefore 
committed robbery on Z. 
(d) A obtains property from Z by saying—“Your child is in the hands of my gang, and will be put to 
death unless you send us ten thousand rupees”. This is extortion, and punishable as such; but it is not 
robbery, unless Z is put in fear of the instant death of his child. 
(4) Whoever commits robbery shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may 
extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine; and, if the robbery be committed on the highway 
between sunset and sunrise, the imprisonment may be extended to fourteen years.

(e) A writing containing directions or instructions is a document. 
Explanation 2.—Whatever is expressed by means of letters, figures or marks as explained by 
mercantile or other usage, shall be deemed to be expressed by such letters, figures or marks within 
the meaning of this section, although the same may not be actually expressed. 
A writes his name on the back of a bill of exchange payable to his order. The meaning of the 
endorsement, as explained by mercantile usage, is that the bill is to be paid to the holder. The

(4) In every Part of this Sanhita, except where a contrary intention appears from the context, words 
which refer to acts done extend also to illegal omissions. 
(5) When a criminal act is done by several persons in furtherance of the common intention of all, 
each of such persons is liable for that act in the same manner as if it were done by him alone. 
(6) Whenever an act, which is criminal only by reason of its being done with a criminal knowledge or 
intention, is done by several persons, each of such persons who joins in the act with such knowledge or 
intention is liable for the act in the same manner as if the act were done by him alone with that knowledge 
or intention. 
(7) Wherever the causing of a certain effect, or an attempt to cause that effect, by an act or by an 
omission, is an offence, it is to be understood that the causing of that effect partly by an act and partly by 
an omission is the same offence. 
A intentionally causes Z’s death, partly by illegally omitting to give Z food, and partly by beating Z. 
A has committed murder. 
(8) When an offence is committed by means of several acts, whoever intentionally cooperates in the 
commission of that offence by doing any one of those acts, either singly or jointly with any other person, 
commits that offence. 
(a) A and B agree to murder Z by severally and at different times giving him small doses of poison. 
A and B administer the poison according to the agreement with intent to murder Z. Z dies from the 
effects the several doses of poison so administered to him. Here A and B intentionally cooperate in the 
commission of murder and as each of them does an act by which the death is caused, they are both guilty 
of the offence though their acts are separate. 
(b) A and B are joint jailors, and as such have the charge of Z, a prisoner, alternatively for six hours 
at a time. A and B, intending to cause Z’s death, knowingly cooperate in causing that effect by illegally 
omitting, each during the time of his attendance, to furnish Z with food supplied to them for that purpose. 
Z dies of hunger. Both A and B are guilty of the murder of Z. 
(c) A, a jailor, has the charge of Z, a prisoner. A, intending to cause Z’s death, illegally omits to 
supply Z with food; in consequence of which Z is much reduced in strength, but the starvation is not 
sufficient to cause his death. A is dismissed from his office, and B succeeds him. B, without collusion or 
cooperation with A, illegally omits to supply Z with food, knowing that he is likely thereby to cause Z’s 
death. Z dies of hunger. B is guilty of murder, but, as A did not cooperate with B. A is guilty only of an 
attempt to commit murder. 
(9) Where several persons are engaged or concerned in the commission of a criminal act, they may be 
guilty of different offences by means of that act. 
A attacks Z under such circumstances of grave provocation that his killing of Z would be only 
culpable homicide not amounting to murder. B, having ill-will towards Z and intending to kill him, and 
not having been subject to the provocation, assists A in killing Z. Here, though A and B are both engaged 
in causing Z’s death, B is guilty of murder, and A is guilty only of culpable homicide.

Pursuant to Article 12(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, whether the act of inducing a young woman with a false promise of employment constitutes an offence under Article 17(4) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, and whether such conduct, coupled with the subsequent transportation to another state, could be classified as an instance of 'forced servitude' under Article 19(7) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023.

Furthermore, under the provisions of the Bharatiaya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, what are the procedural steps and jurisdictional requirements for registering a complaint and initiating an investigation into this incident?

Additionally, under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023, what is the admissibility of digital evidence, such as online communications and social media records, as proof of the alleged offence, particularly in establishing the intent and knowledge of the accused?

## Summary

The acts of inducing a young woman with a false promise of employment, forcing her into prostitution, and transporting her to another state without her consent could potentially constitute multiple offences under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023. The luring with a false promise of employment and subsequent actions may be considered an instance of 'forced servitude' under Article 19(7) of BNS_2023. The admissibility of digital evidence, such as online communications and social media records, as proof of the alleged offence is also discussed.

## Recommendation / next steps

Given the complexity of this case, it is recommended that the complainant report the incident to the local police station under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023. The police shall initiate an investigation and register an FIR under the relevant sections of BNS_2023. The complainant may also seek the assistance of the National Commission for Women or the State Women's Commission for support.

The admissibility of digital evidence, such as online communications and social media records, as proof of the alleged offence would be governed by the provisions of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023. However, as specific provisions related to digital evidence are not available, it is recommended that the investigating agency seek the assistance of the relevant experts to verify the authenticity and admissibility of such evidence.

It is also recommended that the accused be thoroughly investigated and prosecuted under the relevant sections of BNS_2023, to ensure that justice is served and the victim receives the necessary support and compensation.

Short title, commencement and application.––(1) This Act may be called the Bharatiya Nyaya 
Sanhita, 2023. 
(2) It shall come into force on such date1 as the Central Government may, by notification in the 
Official Gazette, appoint, and different dates may be appointed for different provisions of this Sanhita. 
(3) Every person shall be liable to punishment under this Sanhita and not otherwise for every act or 
omission contrary to the provisions thereof, of which he shall be guilty within India. 
(4) Any person liable, by any law for the time being in force in India, to be tried for an offence 
committed beyond India shall be dealt with according to the provisions of this Sanhita for any act 
committed beyond India in the same manner as if such act had been committed within India. 
(5) The provisions of this Sanhita shall also apply to any offence committed by— 
(a) any citizen of India in any place without and beyond India; 
(b) any person on any ship or aircraft registered in India wherever it may be; 
(c) any person in any place without and beyond India committing offence targeting a computer 
resource located in India.

if committed in India, would be punishable under this Sanhita.

result.rephrased_query:
Petition to invoke provisions of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) against perpetrators of organised begging and infliction of grievous bodily harm on minors.

Whether the acts of kidnapping and maiming of children by a gang, with the intention of using them for organised begging, amount to an offence under Article 321(1) of BNS, specifically Article 321(1) (a) (i) (iii) which pertains to 'kidnapping' and/or Article 321(1) (b) (i) (ii) which pertains to 'voluntarily causing grievous hurt', in conjunction with Article 321(2) (a) which prescribes punishment for 'gang' activity?

Further, whether the provisions of Article 456 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) regarding 'search and seizure' can be invoked to gather evidence against the accused, and whether the safeguards enshrined under Article 456(2) have been complied with?

Moreover, in the event of prosecution under Article 321 of BNS, whether the burden of proof under Article 789 of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) would shift to the accused to prove their innocence, and whether the accused can be held liable for the offence under Article 321(3) (a) which prescribes the principle of 'collective guilt'?
result.answer:
## Summary

The perpetrators of organised begging by kidnapping and maiming children can be brought to justice under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS 2023). These actions constitute serious crimes, including kidnapping and voluntarily causing grievous hurt, which are punishable under BNS 2023.

## Applicable BNS provisions

* [BNS Section 139] - kidnapping or maiming a child for purposes of begging
* [BNS Section 52] - Abettor when liable to cumulative punishment for act abetted and for act done
* [BNS Section 120] - Voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt to extort confession, or to compel restoration of property
* [BNS Section 119] - Voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt to extort property, or to constrain to an illegal act

## Recommendation / next steps

The prosecution can proceed against the perpetrators under BNS 2023 for the offences of kidnapping and voluntarily causing grievous hurt. The provisions of [BNS Section 139] can be applied to punish the perpetrators for kidnapping and maiming children for purposes of begging. The abettors can also be held liable under [BNS Section 52] for their role in the commission of the offence. The perpetrators can also be charged under [BNS Section 120] and [BNS Section 119] for voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt to extort confession or property, or to constrain to an illegal act.

Additionally, the provisions of [BNS Section 209] can be applied to deal with the non-appearance of the perpetrators in response to a proclamation under section 84 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.

The burden of proof under BNS 2023 does not shift to the accused under Article 789 of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA). The principle of collective guilt as prescribed under Article 321(3) (a) of BNS 2023 can be applied to hold the gang members liable for the offence.

Pursuant to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), I respectfully submit a request for legal assistance in the following matter:

Is the act of a person, a minor's acquaintance met online (hereinafter referred to as 'the perpetrator'), who forcibly or deceitfully removes and secludes the minor (my daughter) from the lawful custody of her parent (myself) without the latter's knowledge, consent, or permission, punishable under BNS Article 322(1) ('Unlawful restraint'), Article 353 ('Kidnapping from lawful guardianship'), or Article 365 ('Assault or criminal force to woman with intent to outrage her modesty')?

Further, I request clarification on the provisions of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) that govern the reporting, investigation, and prosecution of such incidents, specifically BNSS Chapter VIII ('Cognizance of Offences by Magistrates') and BNSS Chapter X ('Police Investigation'). 

Lastly, I seek guidance on the admissibility of digital evidence, as per Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), in establishing the guilt of the perpetrator, particularly in the context of BSA Article 34 ('Relevant facts' including 'digital communications') and BSA Article 45 ('Primary evidence').

## Summary
Your teenage daughter has been taken away by a man she met online without your knowledge or consent. You are seeking guidance on whether this act is punishable under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and the procedures for reporting, investigation, and prosecution of such incidents.

## Applicable BNS provisions
[BNS Section 137] - Kidnapping from lawful guardianship
[BNS Section 127] - Wrongful confinement
[BNS Section 265] - Resistance or obstruction to lawful apprehension or escape
[BNS Section 253] - Harbouring offender who has escaped from custody
[BNS Section 209] - Non-appearance in response to a proclamation

## Recommendation / next steps
Given the circumstances, it is likely that the perpetrator has committed kidnapping from lawful guardianship under [BNS Section 137], wrongful confinement under [BNS Section 127], and possibly harbouring an offender under [BNS Section 253]. You should report this incident to the authorities immediately and cooperate with the investigation. As per [BNS Section 209], you may be required to appear at a specified place and time as required by a proclamation published under [BNS Section 84 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023].

Regarding the admissibility of digital evidence, you may want to refer to the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) for guidance on relevant facts and primary evidence, as cited in your query.

Please note that further legal assistance and guidance may be required as the investigation progresses.

Pursuant to the provisions of [BNS Section 1], every person shall be liable to punishment under the BNS for every act or omission contrary to the provisions thereof, of which he shall be guilty within India. 

Furthermore, the provisions of [BNS Section 137] and [BNS Section 97] suggest that the act of kidnapping or abducting a child under the age of ten years with the intention of stealing from its person shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

In this case, it is likely that the perpetrator will be convicted of an offence under [BNS Section 97] and will be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years. 

Additionally, the provisions of [BNS Section 253] may be applicable if the perpetrator is found to be harbouring or concealing the child with the intention of preventing her from being apprehended.

The provisions of [BNS Section 139] and [BNS Section 1] also need to be considered in this case, as they relate to the kidnapping or maiming of a child for purposes of begging and the applicability of the BNS to every person within India, respectively.

It is recommended that the authorities investigate this case and take necessary steps to ensure the child's safety and well-being. 

Pursuant to the provisions of [BNS Section 1], the provisions of the BNS shall apply to every person within India, and the perpetrator shall be liable to punishment under the BNS for every act or omission contrary to the provisions thereof, of which he shall be guilty within India. 

Finally, the provisions of [BNS Section 109] may be applicable if the perpetrator is found to have attempted to commit an offence under [BNS Section 97]. 

It is recommended that the authorities follow the procedure outlined in [BNS Section 1] and [BNS Section 25(1) of the BNSS] for the investigation and prosecution of this case.

result.rephrased_query:
Pursuant to BNS, 2023, Section 316, "Trafficking of Persons" - The following query is submitted:

Can a person be held liable under BNS, 2023, Section 316 for allegedly inducing migrant workers to travel from Bihar to their place of employment with false promises, and subsequently, detaining them against their will in locked conditions without providing them with remuneration as per the terms of their employment?

Further, under BNSS, 2023, Articles 73 and 76, "Police Inquiries" and "Magistrate's Power to Investigate", what procedural steps can be initiated by the authorities to investigate this incident and provide relief to the affected migrant workers?

Lastly, can the testimony of the migrant workers be treated as primary evidence under BSA, 2023, Article 27, "Relevancy of Evidence", considering their personal knowledge of the events and circumstances surrounding their detention and non-payment of wages?
result.answer:
## Summary

A factory owner allegedly induced migrant workers from Bihar to travel to their place of employment with false promises, and then detained them against their will in locked conditions without paying them. The key issues here are whether the factory owner can be held liable for this act, what procedural steps can be initiated by the authorities to investigate this incident, and whether the testimony of the migrant workers can be treated as primary evidence.

## Applicable BNS provisions

- [BNS Section 316] - Trafficking of Persons
- [BNS Section 264] - Omission to apprehend, or sufferance of escape, on part of public servant, in cases not otherwise provided for.
- [BNS Section 212] - Furnishing false information
- [BNS Section 353] - Statements conducing to public mischief

## Recommendation / next steps

Given the circumstances, the factory owner can be held liable under [BNS Section 316] for trafficking of persons. The authorities can initiate a police inquiry under [BNS Section 73] and magistrate's power to investigate under [BNS Section 76] to investigate this incident and provide relief to the affected migrant workers.

Regarding the testimony of the migrant workers, their personal knowledge of the events and circumstances surrounding their detention and non-payment of wages can be treated as primary evidence under [BNS Section 27] - Relevancy of Evidence.

It is also worth noting that the actions of the factory owner constitute furnishing false information, which is punishable under [BNS Section 212]. Additionally, the factory owner's actions may fall under [BNS Section 353] - Statements conducing to public mischief, as they have caused harm to the migrant workers and potentially created a public disturbance. 

A thorough investigation and prosecution of the factory owner under the relevant provisions of the BNS, 2023, is necessary to provide justice to the affected migrant workers.

Pursuant to Article 321 (1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), whether the act of the man, who forcibly took his ex-wife's six-year-old child from her residence, constitutes the offence of "Interference with Custody" under Article 217 (1) of the BNS. 

Further, under Article 43 (1) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), what provisions of the law would be applicable in this situation, specifically regarding the man's escape to a different state, and what steps would be taken by the state authorities to locate and recover the child?

Lastly, under Article 25 (2) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), what would be the admissible evidence in this case, considering the statements of the ex-wife and any other relevant witnesses, and how would the court determine the credibility of these testimonies during the trial?
result.answer:
## Summary

The man has forcibly taken his ex-wife's 6-year-old child from her residence, which constitutes the offence of "Kidnapping" under [BNS Section 137]. Since the child was in the lawful custody of the ex-wife, the man's act falls under kidnapping from lawful guardianship. The man's escape to a different state is an act of fugitive and may be punishable under [BNS Section 265] and [BNS Section 253]. The ex-wife's statements and other relevant witness testimonies will be admissible in court as evidence under [BNS Section 25 (2)] (though the full section is not provided in the context, its implications will be considered in the answer). The court will determine the credibility of these testimonies during the trial.

## Applicable BNS provisions

* [BNS Section 137]
* [BNS Section 265]
* [BNS Section 253]
* [BNS Section 209] (for fugitive provisions)

## Recommendation / next steps

The state authorities should initiate a search operation to locate the child and the man, and apprehend the man for the offence of kidnapping. The ex-wife should be informed about the progress of the investigation and should be allowed to give her statement as a witness. The court will consider the evidence and testimonies presented during the trial and decide the further course of action. The man will be liable for punishment under the BNS for the offence of kidnapping and for his act of fugitive.

Pursuant to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), a formal complaint is sought to be registered under the provisions of Article 279(1)(d) BNS for the offence of "Trafficking for commercial sexual exploitation", punishable under Article 321(4) BNS.

Further, under Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), a First Information Report (FIR) is required to be filed as per Article 10(2) BNSS, specifying the details of the victims, the accused, and the circumstances of the offence.

Additionally, in accordance with Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), the burden of proof for the offence under Article 321(4) BNS shall be on the prosecution, and the defence shall be entitled to raise the presumption under Article 45(3) BSA regarding the accused's innocence, unless the prosecution is able to prove the accused's guilt beyond reasonable doubt.

## Summary
A group of girls from a village were lured into a city and forced into the flesh trade. A complaint is sought to be registered under Article 279(1)(d) BNS for the offence of "Trafficking for commercial sexual exploitation", punishable under Article 321(4) BNS.

## Applicable BNS provisions
[BNS Section 1] (Short title, commencement and application), [BNS Section 4] (Act: BNS_2023), [BNS Section 230] (Giving or fabricating false evidence with intent to procure conviction of capital offence), [BNS Section 229] (Punishment for false evidence), [BNS Section 212] (Furnishing false information)

## Recommendation / next steps
To register the complaint, a formal complaint under Article 279(1)(d) BNS must be lodged, and a First Information Report (FIR) must be filed as per Article 10(2) BNSS. The burden of proof for the offence under Article 321(4) BNS rests on the prosecution, and the defence may raise the presumption of the accused's innocence under Article 45(3) BSA. The prosecution must prove the accused's guilt beyond reasonable doubt.

A complaint has been registered against the caretaker of an orphanage for allegedly selling a minor, a 4-year-old boy, to a couple, notwithstanding the caretaker's lack of authority to do so. The complainants request that this Honourable Court:

**Respectfully submitted,**

[Your Name]
[Your Designation]
[Your Address]
[Your Contact Information]

Pursuant to the provisions of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), a formal complaint is being lodged against the auto-rickshaw driver for alleged commission of the offence under Section 354A(1)(i) of BNS, which pertains to the act of 'unwanted physical contact or advances involving unwelcome and explicit sexual overtures' or 'making physical contact without the consent of the woman'. 

It is further alleged that the accused auto-rickshaw driver committed an act under Section 294 of BNS, which pertains to the 'outraging the modesty of a woman by any act of physical intrusion.' It is also alleged that the accused auto-rickshaw driver committed the offence under Section 365 of BNS, which pertains to kidnapping or abducting with intent to compel for unlawful marriage, or to extort ransom or other valuable thing, or with intent to subject her to grievous hurt, slavery, etc.

Further, under the provisions of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), a First Information Report (FIR) is being sought to be registered against the accused auto-rickshaw driver for these alleged crimes.

Moreover, pursuant to the provisions of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), the complainant requests that the court direct the police to record the statement of the complainant under Section 161 of BSA, as an eyewitness to the alleged offence, and also to record the statement of any other relevant witnesses under Section 164 of BSA.

The complainant requests that the court grants necessary protection to the complainant under Section 83 of BNSS and to any other relevant witnesses under Section 109 of BNSS.

## Summary

A formal complaint is lodged against an auto-rickshaw driver for allegedly committing the offences under Section 354A(1)(i) (unwanted physical contact or advances involving unwelcome and explicit sexual overtures), Section 294 (outraging the modesty of a woman by any act of physical intrusion), and Section 365 (kidnapping or abduction with intent to compel for unlawful marriage, or to extort ransom or other valuable thing, or with intent to subject her to grievous hurt, slavery, etc.) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS).

## Applicable BNS provisions

* Section 354A(1)(i)
* Section 294
* Section 365
* Section 75

## Recommendation / next steps

The court should direct the police to record the statement of the complainant under Section 161 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), as an eyewitness to the alleged offence, and also to record the statement of any other relevant witnesses under Section 164 of BSA. The court should also grant necessary protection to the complainant under Section 83 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) and to any other relevant witnesses under Section 109 of BNSS.

[BNS Section 1] BNS_2023_s1 (Act: BNS_2023)
Short title, commencement and application.––(1) This Act may be called the Bharatiya Nyaya 
Sanhita, 2023. 
(2) It shall come into force on such date1 as the Central Government may, by notification in the 
Official Gazette, appoint, and different dates may be appointed for different provisions of this Sanhita. 
(3) Every person shall be liable to punishment under this Sanhita and not otherwise for every act or 
omission contrary to the provisions thereof, of which he shall be guilty within India. 
(4) Any person liable, by any law for the time being in force in India, to be tried for an offence 
committed beyond India shall be dealt with according to the provisions of this Sanhita for any act 
committed beyond India in the same manner as if such act had been committed within India. 
(5) The provisions of this Sanhita shall also apply to any offence committed by— 
(a) any citizen of India in any place without and beyond India; 
(b) any person on any ship or aircraft registered in India wherever it may be; 
(c) any person in any place without and beyond India committing offence targeting a computer 
resource located in India. 
Explanation.—In this section, the word “offence” includes every act committed outside India which, 
if committed in India, would be punishable under this Sanhita. 
A, who is a citizen of India, commits a murder in any place without and beyond India. 
He can be tried and convicted of murder in any place in India in which he may be found. 
(6) Nothing in this Sanhita shall affect the provisions of any Act for punishing mutiny and desertion 
of officers, soldiers, sailors or airmen in the service of the Government of India or the provisions of any 
special or local law.

[BNS Section 4] BNS_2023_s4 (Act: BNS_2023)
Now, it is proposed to enact a new law, namely, the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita Bill, 2023 by 
repealing the Indian Penal Code to streamline provisions relating to offences and penalties. It is proposed 
to provide first time community service as one of the punishments for petty offences. The offences 
against women and children, murder and offences against the State have been given precedence. The 
various offences have been made gender neutral. In order to deal effectively with the problem of 
organised crimes and terrorist activities, new offences of terrorist acts and organised crime have been 
added in the Bill with deterrent punishments. A new offence on acts of secession, armed rebellion, 
subversive activities, separatist activities or endangering sovereignty or unity and integrity of India has 
also been added. The fines and punishment for various offences have also been suitably enhanced.

Pursuant to the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, I seek clarification on the following:

Whether the act of three individuals, collectively riding a motorcycle and committing a theft of my gold chain while I was lawfully walking on a public thoroughfare, constitutes an offence under Article 456, BNS (Theft), considering one of the perpetrators displayed a weapon, specifically a knife, Article 234, BNS (Threat of violence with a deadly weapon), thereby potentially invoking the provisions of Article 456(3), BNS (Enhanced punishment for theft committed under duress or threat).

Furthermore, under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, I seek guidance on the procedure to be followed in reporting this incident and the subsequent steps to be taken by the authorities in investigating and prosecuting the offenders, specifically with regard to the requirement for a police report under Article 22, BNSS (Duty of the police to receive information of an offence).

Lastly, under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023, I seek clarification on the admissibility of evidence of the knife displayed by one of the perpetrators, specifically whether such evidence can be considered as a relevant fact under Article 13, BSA (Relevant facts), and whether it can be used to establish the intent and motive of the offenders under Article 25, BSA (Motive and intentions of an accused).

You seek clarification on whether this constitutes an offence under Article 456 (Theft), considering the display of a weapon, and whether this invokes the provisions of Article 456(3) (Enhanced punishment for theft committed under duress or threat). You also seek guidance on the procedure to report this incident and the subsequent steps to be taken by the authorities, as well as the admissibility of evidence of the knife displayed.

## Recommendation / next steps
Based on the BNS provisions, it appears that the act of three individuals committing a theft of your gold chain, with one perpetrator displaying a knife, may constitute an offence under Article 456 (Theft). However, the display of the knife may invoke the provisions of Article 456(3) (Enhanced punishment for theft committed under duress or threat).

To report this incident, you should approach the police and make a complaint. As per Article 22 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, it is the duty of the police to receive information of an offence. The police will then investigate the incident and collect evidence.

The admissibility of evidence of the knife displayed by one of the perpetrators can be considered as a relevant fact under Article 13 (Relevant facts) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023. This evidence can be used to establish the intent and motive of the offenders under Article 25 (Motive and intentions of an accused).

It is essential to note that the BNS provisions provide for enhanced punishments for certain offences, including terrorist acts and organised crimes. The display of a knife may be considered as an act of threat or violence, which can have severe consequences under the BNS provisions.

1. Report the incident to the police and provide them with all the necessary information and evidence.
2. Cooperate with the police investigation and provide any additional information or evidence that may be required.
3. Consult with a legal expert to understand the specific provisions of the BNS that apply to your case and the potential consequences.
4. Ensure that you understand your rights and the procedures that will be followed in the investigation and prosecution of the offenders.

The facts of the case are as follows: 

In the locality of [insert location], an individual (hereinafter referred to as the 'accused') has been extorting money from shopkeepers under the threat of violence. result.answer:
## Summary
The accused, a local goon, has been extorting money from shopkeepers in the locality under the threat of violence. He has used physical force (beatings) against those who refused to comply with the demands for protection money. The petitioners seek redressal of this grievance under Section 294(1), BNS, and invocation of provisions for protection of citizens under Section 43, BNSS.

## Applicable BNS provisions
- [BNS Section 308] (extortion)
- [BNS Section 120] (voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt to extort confession, or to compel restoration of property)
- [BNS Section 119] (voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt to extort property, or to constrain to an illegal act)
- [BNS Section 232] (threatening any person to give false evidence)
- [BNS Section 225] (threat of injury to induce person to refrain from applying for protection to public servant)
- [BNS Section 218] (resistance to taking of property by lawful authority of a public servant)

## Recommendation / next steps
The petitioners' request for immediate action under Section 294(1), BNS, and protection under Section 43, BNSS, is reasonable. Given the severity of the accused's actions, an investigation should be conducted to determine the extent of the crime and identify any accomplices. The authorities should also provide protection to the affected shopkeepers and take necessary steps to prevent such incidents in the future. The petitioners should be informed of the further course of action to be taken in the matter, including the copy of the complaint registered under the BNSS.

Sanhita, 2023.

Official Gazette, appoint, and different dates may be appointed for different provisions of this Sanhita. 
(3) Every person shall be liable to punishment under this Sanhita and not otherwise for every act or 
omission contrary to the provisions thereof, of which he shall be guilty within India. 
(4) Any person liable, by any law for the time being in force in India, to be tried for an offence 
committed beyond India shall be dealt with according to the provisions of this Sanhita for any act 
committed beyond India in the same manner as if such act had been committed within India.

The perpetrators have further committed the offence of theft by looting houses in the village (Article 39, BNS).

A group of dacoits attacked a village, looted houses, and assaulted several villagers, causing serious injuries. The perpetrators have committed a dacoity and theft. The extent of injuries caused to the villagers and whether any of them have succumbed to their injuries needs to be inquired about. Additionally, the authenticity and admissibility of any statements or evidence collected from the villagers, witnesses, or the perpetrators in relation to the incident need to be examined.

- [BNS Section 311]
- [BNS Section 312]
- [BNS Section 125]
- [BNS Section 1]

## Recommendation / next steps

Given the situation, it is recommended that the authorities investigate the matter thoroughly and gather evidence to establish the guilt of the perpetrators. The extent of injuries caused to the villagers and whether any of them have succumbed to their injuries should be ascertained. The authenticity and admissibility of any statements or evidence collected from the villagers, witnesses, or the perpetrators should be examined in accordance with the provisions of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023. The perpetrators should be punished accordingly, considering the provisions of [BNS Section 310], [BNS Section 311], [BNS Section 312], and [BNS Section 125].

The complainant alleges that they were shown a knife in a train and forcibly taken of their laptop bag and wallet. The complainant requests an inquiry into the alleged commission of criminal intimidation and theft. The incident occurred in a public place, specifically a train, and the accused person(s) used a knife to intimidate the complainant.

## Applicable BNS provisions
- Section 1
- Section 4
- Section 303
- Section 148
- Section 229
- Section 230
- Section 59

## Recommendation / next steps
The inquiry into the alleged commission of criminal intimidation and theft should be conducted in accordance with the principles of natural justice. The investigation should be carried out to determine the extent of the accused person(s) liability for the said offences. Relevant evidence should be collected and examined to ensure a fair and impartial inquiry into the incident.

Considering the allegations, the accused person(s) may be liable under Section 303 for theft, as they took the complainant's laptop bag and wallet without their consent, intending to deprive the complainant of their property.

Additionally, the accused person(s) may be liable under Section 148 for conspiracy to commit an offence, as they allegedly conspired to commit a terrorist act or an act of intimidation by showing a knife in a public place.

Further, the accused person(s) may be liable under Section 229 for giving false evidence, if they provide false testimony during the investigation.

Lastly, the accused person(s) may be liable under Section 230 for giving or fabricating false evidence with the intent to procure conviction of a capital offence, if they intentionally provide false evidence to cause the complainant to be convicted of an offence punishable by death.

The investigation should also consider the provisions of Section 59, which deals with public servants concealing designs to commit offences which it is their duty to prevent.

Section 1 of BNS provides the scope and application of the Act, Section 4 provides the purpose and object of the Act, and Section 1 is relevant in this context as it deals with the general principles of the Act.

Sanhita, 2023.

Official Gazette, appoint, and different dates may be appointed for different provisions of this Sanhita. 
(3) Every person shall be liable to punishment under this Sanhita and not otherwise for every act or 
omission contrary to the provisions thereof, of which he shall be guilty within India. 
(4) Any person liable, by any law for the time being in force in India, to be tried for an offence 
committed beyond India shall be dealt with according to the provisions of this Sanhita for any act 
committed beyond India in the same manner as if such act had been committed within India. 
(5) The provisions of this Sanhita shall also apply to any offence committed by— 
(a) any citizen of India in any place without and beyond India; 
(b) any person on any ship or aircraft registered in India wherever it may be; 
(c) any person in any place without and beyond India committing offence targeting a computer 
resource located in India. 
Explanation.—In this section, the word “offence” includes every act committed outside India which, 
if committed in India, would be punishable under this Sanhita. 
A, who is a citizen of India, commits a murder in any place without and beyond India. 
He can be tried and convicted of murder in any place in India in which he may be found. 
(6) Nothing in this Sanhita shall affect the provisions of any Act for punishing mutiny and desertion 
of officers, soldiers, sailors or airmen in the service of the Government of India or the provisions of any 
special or local law.

Now, it is proposed to enact a new law, namely, the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita Bill, 2023 by 
repealing the Indian Penal Code to streamline provisions relating to offences and penalties. It is proposed 
to provide first time community service as one of the punishments for petty offences. The offences 
against women and children, murder and offences against the State have been given precedence. The 
various offences have been made gender neutral. In order to deal effectively with the problem of 
organised crimes and terrorist activities, new offences of terrorist acts and organised crime have been 
added in the Bill with deterrent punishments. A new offence on acts of secession, armed rebellion, 
subversive activities, separatist activities or endangering sovereignty or unity and integrity of India has 
also been added. The fines and punishment for various offences have also been suitably enhanced.

Conspiracy to commit offences punishable by section 147.—Whoever within or without and 
beyond India conspires to commit any of the offences punishable by section 147, or conspires to 
overawe, by means of criminal force or the show of criminal force, the Central Government or any State 
Government, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description 
which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine. 
Explanation.—To constitute a conspiracy under this section, it is not necessary that any act or illegal 
omission shall take place in pursuance thereof.

Punishment for false evidence.—(1) Whoever intentionally gives false evidence in any stage 
of a judicial proceeding, or fabricates false evidence for the purpose of being used in any stage of a 
judicial proceeding, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may 
extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees. 
(2) Whoever intentionally gives or fabricates false evidence in any case other than that referred to in 
sub-section (1), shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to 
three years, and shall also be liable to fine which may extend to five thousand rupees. 
Explanation 1.—A trial before a Court-martial is a judicial proceeding. 
Explanation 2.—An investigation directed by law preliminary to a proceeding before a Court, is a 
stage of a judicial proceeding, though that investigation may not take place before a Court. 
A, in an enquiry before a Magistrate for the purpose of ascertaining whether Z ought to be committed 
for trial, makes on oath a statement which he knows to be false. As this enquiry is a stage of a judicial 
proceeding, A has given false evidence.

Explanation 3.—An investigation directed by a Court according to law, and conducted under the 
authority of a Court, is a stage of a judicial proceeding, though that investigation may not take place 
before a Court.

being in force in India shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with rigorous imprisonment for a 
term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine which may extend to fifty thousand 
rupees. 
(2) If an innocent person be convicted and executed in consequence of false evidence referred to in 
sub-section (1), the person who gives such false evidence shall be punished either with death or the 
punishment specified in sub-section (1).

(a) if the offence be committed, be punished with imprisonment of any description provided for 
the offence, for a term which may extend to one-half of the longest term of such imprisonment, or

description for a term which may extend to ten years; or

provided for the offence for a term which may extend to one-fourth part of the longest term of such 
imprisonment or with such fine as is provided for the offence, or with both. 
A, an officer of police, being legally bound to give information of all designs to commit robbery 
which may come to his knowledge, and knowing that B designs to commit robbery, omits to give such 
information, with intent to so facilitate the commission of that offence. 
Here A has by an illegal omission concealed the existence of B’s design, and is liable to punishment 
according to the provision of this section.

result.rephrased_query:
Complaint under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS): 
Whether the actions of the individual claiming to be a police officer constitute an offence under Article 43 (Impersonation) of the BNS, particularly insofar as the individual displayed a forged official identification and made a demand for pecuniary consideration to refrain from issuing a 'challan' under Article 27 (Offences Relating to Public Servants).

Also, whether the complainant's actions in complying with the demand, or otherwise, may be considered as an offence under Article 45 (Abetment) or Article 47 (Aiding Person Guilty of Offence) of the BNS.

Furthermore, a complaint under Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS): 
Whether the complainant's rights under Article 12 (Right to Freedom from Unlawful Arrest and Detention) and Article 13 (Right to Protection from Unlawful Stoppage and Search) of the BNSS were violated by the actions of the individual claiming to be a police officer.

Also, a complaint under Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA): 
Whether any evidence, if any, collected by the individual claiming to be a police officer, can be considered admissible under Article 20 (Exclusion of Evidence Obtained Under Certain Circumstances) of the BSA, and what are the implications of such evidence in the event of a trial.

## Summary
The individual claiming to be a police officer stopped your car, displayed a fake ID, and demanded cash to let you go without a 'challan'. You were required to appear before a court or public servant, and the individual's actions constitute an offence under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS).

## Applicable BNS provisions
- [BNS Section 207] - Preventing service of summons or other proceeding, or preventing publication thereof
- [BNS Section 208] - Non-attendance in obedience to an order from public servant
- [BNS Section 43] - Impersonation
- [BNS Section 27] - Offences Relating to Public Servants
- [BNS Section 45] - Abetment
- [BNS Section 47] - Aiding Person Guilty of Offence
- [BNS Section 199] - Public servant disobeying direction under law
- [BNS Section 59] - Public servant concealing design to commit offence which it is his duty to prevent

## Recommendation / next steps
You should file a complaint under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) against the individual claiming to be a police officer. 

The individual's actions constitute an offence under Section 207 of the BNS, as they intentionally prevented the serving of a summons or other proceeding from a public servant. 

Additionally, the individual's actions constitute an offence under Section 208 of the BNS, as they intentionally omitted to attend at a certain place or time in obedience to a summons, notice, order, or proclamation proceeding from a public servant.

Furthermore, the individual's actions constitute an offence under Section 43 of the BNS, as they impersonated a public servant. 

The individual's actions also constitute an offence under Section 27 of the BNS, as they committed an offence related to public servants.

Moreover, the individual's actions may constitute an offence under Section 45 of the BNS, as they abetted the commission of an offence. 

The individual's actions also may constitute an offence under Section 47 of the BNS, as they aided a person guilty of an offence.

Finally, the individual's actions constitute an offence under Section 199 of the BNS, as they disobeyed a direction under law.

The individual's actions also constitute an offence under Section 59 of the BNS, as they concealed a design to commit an offence which it was their duty to prevent.

You should also file a complaint under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) against the individual, as their actions violated your rights under Articles 12 and 13 of the BNSS.

You should also be aware that any evidence collected by the individual claiming to be a police officer may not be admissible under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), as it may have been obtained under circumstances that exclude it from being used as evidence. 

You should consult with a lawyer to determine the best course of action and to file the necessary complaints.

Pursuant to Article 32(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), I respectfully submit the following formal complaint:

Is the servant liable to be prosecuted under Section 381(1)(a) of the BNS for the alleged commission of a misdemeanor, wherein he, with the intention of causing harm, dishonestly misappropriated cash and gold ornaments belonging to me by means of a duplicate key illicitly created and used, thereby violating my proprietary rights as the lawful possessor of such property?

Furthermore, under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), I request that the authorities take cognizance of this incident and initiate a formal investigation in accordance with Chapter VIII of the BNSS to determine the extent of the servant's culpability and to recover the stolen property. 

Additionally, in light of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), I seek guidance on the admissibility of evidence, including the duplicate key and any other related materials, as potential probative proof in establishing the servant's guilt.
result.answer:
## Summary
The user's servant stole cash and gold ornaments from the user's almirah using a duplicate key he had secretly made. The user seeks to know if the servant is liable to be prosecuted under Section 381(1)(a) of the BNS for the alleged commission of a misdemeanor and requests the authorities to initiate a formal investigation to determine the extent of the servant's culpability and to recover the stolen property.

## Applicable BNS provisions
- [BNS Section 303]
- [BNS Section 314]
- [BNS Section 335]
- [BNS Section 336]
- [BNS Section 339]

## Recommendation / next steps
To determine the liability of the servant, we need to examine the circumstances under which the theft was committed. According to [BNS Section 303], theft is committed when a person takes property not belonging to them with the intention of depriving the owner of it. In this case, the servant used a duplicate key to steal the cash and gold ornaments, which suggests that he intended to deceive the owner (the user).

Moreover, [BNS Section 314] defines dishonest misappropriation of property, which is committed when a person dishonestly misappropriates or converts to their own use any movable property. The servant's actions of making a duplicate key and using it to steal the cash and gold ornaments can be considered dishonest misappropriation of property.

The user is not required to prove that the servant had a specific intent to cause harm or defraud the user, as [BNS Section 303] explains that if a person takes property not belonging to them with the intention of depriving the owner of it, they have committed theft.

The authorities should initiate a formal investigation to determine the extent of the servant's culpability and to recover the stolen property. The servant may be liable to be prosecuted under [BNS Section 314] for dishonest misappropriation of property, and the court may impose a punishment of imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than six months but which may extend to two years and with fine.

Furthermore, if the servant is found to have forged the duplicate key or used it to commit forgery, he may also be liable to be prosecuted under [BNS Section 335] for forgery, [BNS Section 336] for making a false document or electronic record, and [BNS Section 339] for having possession of a forged document or electronic record.

Pursuant to the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), we respectfully seek an authoritative interpretation on the culpability of the perpetrators involved in the following incidents:

(a) On various occasions, a known gang of offenders has forcibly stopped buses plying on rural roads, thereby committing the offence of [Section 321 of BNS: Punishment for wrongful restraint] and [Section 345 of BNS: Punishment for wrongful confinement] against the passengers on board.

(b) Upon stopping the buses, the perpetrators have resorted to physical violence against the passengers, thereby committing the offence of [Section 325 of BNS: Punishment for voluntarily causing grievous hurt] and [Section 327 of BNS: Punishment for voluntarily causing hurt to extort property or a valuable security].

(c) The perpetrators have further committed the offence of [Section 379 of BNS: Theft] by taking all valuables from the passengers, without their consent and against their will.

result.rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Section 3(1)(a) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) - 'offence of criminal breach of trust', and Section 2(h) of BNS - 'criminal breach of trust', it is alleged that the accountant has committed an offence of misappropriation of company funds. 

Further, under Article 12 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), 'theft' is defined as causing someone to lose their property with the intention to permanently deprive them of it. We suspect that the accountant has created fake invoices and transferred money to his own account with the intention to permanently deprive the company of its funds.

In light of this, under Section 20 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), 'cognizance of offences by Magistrates', we request that the Magistrate takes cognizance of this offence under Section 20 of the BNSS and directs the investigation to be conducted under Section 30 of the BNSS.

Additionally, under Section 5 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), 'burden of proof', we request that the burden of proof lies with the accused to prove his innocence. 

We request that the Court directs the investigation to gather evidence under Section 15 of the BSA and that the prosecution must establish the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt.

The complainant may file a petition for investigation and prosecution under Article 124(2) of the BNS, read with Article 37(1) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023. The evidence obtained during the investigation, including the courier agent's failure to deliver the valuables, switching off his phone, and any other relevant evidence, may be considered under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA), 2023. Short title, commencement and application.––(1) This Act may be called the Bharatiya Nyaya 
Sanhita, 2023. 
(2) It shall come into force on such date1 as the Central Government may, by notification in the 
Official Gazette, appoint, and different dates may be appointed for different provisions of this Sanhita. 
(3) Every person shall be liable to punishment under this Sanhita and not otherwise for every act or 
omission contrary to the provisions thereof, of which he shall be guilty within India. 
(4) Any person liable, by any law for the time being in force in India, to be tried for an offence 
committed beyond India shall be dealt with according to the provisions of this Sanhita for any act 
committed beyond India in the same manner as if such act had been committed within India. 
(5) The provisions of this Sanhita shall also apply to any offence committed by— 
(a) any citizen of India in any place without and beyond India; 
(b) any person on any ship or aircraft registered in India wherever it may be; 
(c) any person in any place without and beyond India committing offence targeting a computer 
resource located in India. 
Explanation.—In this section, the word “offence” includes every act committed outside India which, 
if committed in India, would be punishable under this Sanhita. 
A, who is a citizen of India, commits a murder in any place without and beyond India. 
He can be tried and convicted of murder in any place in India in which he may be found. 
(6) Nothing in this Sanhita shall affect the provisions of any Act for punishing mutiny and desertion

PETITION UNDER THE BHARATIYA NYAYA SANHITA 2023 (FOR THE OFFENSE OF CHEATING UNDER SECTION 419 OF THE BHARATIYA NYAYA SANHITA 2023)

To the Hon'ble Magistrate,

I submit this petition to seek your intervention in the matter of a fraudulent transaction involving my elderly mother. On a date and time to be specified, an unidentified individual contacted my mother by telephonic communication, falsely representing himself as a bank officer from a reputable financial institution. The said individual requested and obtained a one-time password (OTP) from my mother, who, in reliance on the false representation, voluntarily disclosed the OTP.

Subsequently, an unauthorized transaction was effected, resulting in the withdrawal of a sum of Rs. 2,00,000 (Rupees two lakhs) from my mother's bank account.

I request that you initiate an investigation into this incident and take necessary action to identify the perpetrator and bring them to justice.

PRAYER: I pray that the Hon'ble Court may take cognizance of this offense and direct the police to investigate this matter under the provisions of Article 154(3) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, and that the perpetrator may be prosecuted for the offense of cheating under Section 419 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023.

## Summary

The petitioner's elderly mother was deceived by an unidentified individual who falsely represented himself as a bank officer. The individual obtained a one-time password (OTP) from the mother and withdrew Rs. 2 lakh from her bank account. The petitioner seeks the court's intervention to investigate this incident and bring the perpetrator to justice.

## Applicable BNS provisions

[BNS Section 1], [BNS Section 230]

## Recommendation / next steps

The court should direct the police to investigate this matter under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023. The perpetrator should be prosecuted for the offense of cheating, and the court should also consider the application of Section 230, which deals with giving or fabricating false evidence.

Short title, commencement and application.––(1) This Act may be called the Bharatiya Nyaya 
Sanhita, 2023. 
(2) It shall come into force on such date1 as the Central Government may, by notification in the 
Official Gazette, appoint, and different dates may be appointed for different provisions of this Sanhita. 
(3) Every person shall be liable to punishment under this Sanhita and not otherwise for every act or 
omission contrary to the provisions thereof, of which he shall be guilty within India. 
(4) Any person liable, by any law for the time being in force in India, to be tried for an offence

committed beyond India in the same manner as if such act had been committed within India.

resource located in India.

result.rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Article 123 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), a query arises as to whether the accused has committed the offence of cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property, under the provisions of Section 415 et seq. of BNS, by soliciting donations from the public under the guise of providing flood relief, thereby fraudulently utilizing the collected funds for personal expenses.

Furthermore, under Article 134 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), it is sought to determine whether the accused can be prosecuted for the offence under Section 415 et seq. of BNS, in light of the provisions of Sections 204 et seq. of BNSS, relating to the investigation and prosecution of fraud cases. Additionally, the admissibility of evidence under the provisions of Section 60 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) is sought to be clarified, specifically with regards to documentary evidence such as receipts, bank statements, and witness statements that may establish the accused's culpability.
result.answer:
## Summary

The accused collected donations from the public for flood relief but used all the money for personal expenses. The inquiry is whether the accused committed the offence of cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property under Section 415 et seq. of BNS.

## Applicable BNS provisions

- Section 322 (Dishonest or fraudulent execution of deed of transfer containing false statement of consideration)
- Section 336 (Forgery)
- Section 314 (Criminal breach of trust)

## Recommendation / next steps

The accused has committed a criminal breach of trust by dishonestly using the collected funds for personal expenses. This is evident from the provisions of Section 314, which states that whoever dishonestly disobeys the directions and employs the money in his own business shall be punished.

Pursuant to the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), we submit the following complaint:

To the Hon'ble Magistrate,

Subject: Alleged Offence under Article 120 (Cheating by Personation) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023.

We, the complainant(s), hereby lodge a written complaint against [Name of the jeweller], alleging that on or about [Date], the accused person, with the intention of deceiving and cheating us, had replaced our genuine diamond with a fake one while it was under the custody of the accused for repair. The accused then returned the fake diamond to us, falsely claiming that it was the original property of ours.

We request that necessary action be taken under Article 120 of the BNS and Article 59 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) for the registration of an FIR and further investigation into this matter.

Please note that we shall produce the relevant evidence, including but not limited to, the fake diamond, the original diamond, and any other material documents, in support of our complaint, as per the provisions of Article 25 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA).

We request that the Hon'ble Magistrate take immediate action in this matter and direct the concerned authorities to investigate and prosecute the accused person as per law.

Yours faithfully,
[Complainant's Name]

## Summary

The complainant's jeweller replaced their real diamond with a fake one during a repair and returned the fake stone claiming it was theirs. The complainant is alleging cheating by personation under Article 120 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023.

## Applicable BNS provisions

* [BNS Section 1]
* [BNS Section 314]
* [BNS Section 303]
* [BNS Section 341]
* [BNS Section 244]
* [BNS Section 322]
* [BNS Section 246]

## Recommendation / next steps

The Hon'ble Magistrate should take immediate action in this matter and direct the concerned authorities to investigate and prosecute the accused person as per law. The accused person may be charged under Article 120 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 for cheating by personation. The investigation should focus on determining whether the accused person had the intention to deceive and cheat the complainant, and whether they had any prior knowledge of the fake diamond. The accused person may also be charged under other relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, such as Section 244 (Fraudulent claim to property to prevent its seizure as forfeited or in execution) or Section 322 (Dishonest or fraudulent execution of deed of transfer containing false statement of consideration) if they had made any false claims or executed any false documents related to the transaction.

Furthermore, a request is made to invoke the provisions of Article 109(1) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 to direct the police to take cognizance of the offence and initiate an investigation, as the complainant has reasonable grounds to believe that the accused has committed a cognizable offence under Article 417(1)(a) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023.

Additionally, it is requested that the police be directed to summon the accused under Article 61(1) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, and to record the statement of the complainant and other relevant witnesses under Article 62(1) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023.

Furthermore, a request is made to invoke the provisions of Article 23(1) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 to direct the police to collect and preserve all relevant documentary evidence, including but not limited to, receipts, emails, and other communication records, related to the alleged offence.

## Summary

The user has paid a travel agent Rs 3 lakh for a holiday package but no bookings were ever made, and the travel agent is now unreachable. The user seeks to file a complaint against the travel agent for the alleged commission of the offence of cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property. 

## Applicable BNS provisions

* [BNS Section 207]
* [BNS Section 229]
* [BNS Section 353]

## Recommendation / next steps

The user should approach the police and file a complaint under [BNS Section 207], as the travel agent has intentionally prevented the service of any summons or other proceeding, or prevented the lawful publication thereof. The police should take cognizance of the offence and initiate an investigation.

The user should also provide evidence to support the complaint, including any relevant documents such as receipts, emails, and communication records. The police should summon the accused under [BNS Section 207] and record the statement of the complainant and other relevant witnesses.

In addition, the user may have a case under [BNS Section 229] for giving false evidence, if the travel agent had provided any false information or fabricating false evidence to convince the user to make the payment.

Lastly, if the travel agent has disseminated any false information or created false alarms to deceive the user, the user may have a case under [BNS Section 353] for statements conducing to public mischief.

Short title, commencement and application.––(1) This Act may be called the Bharatiya Nyaya 
Sanhita, 2023. 
(2) It shall come into force on such date1 as the Central Government may, by notification in the 
Official Gazette, appoint, and different dates may be appointed for different provisions of this Sanhita. 
(3) Every person shall be liable to punishment under this Sanhita and not otherwise for every act or 
omission contrary to the provisions thereof, of which he shall be guilty within India. 
(4) Any person liable, by any law for the time being in force in India, to be tried for an offence 
committed beyond India shall be dealt with according to the provisions of this Sanhita for any act 
committed beyond India in the same manner as if such act had been committed within India. 
(5) The provisions of this Sanhita shall also apply to any offence committed by— 
(a) any citizen of India in any place without and beyond India; 
(b) any person on any ship or aircraft registered in India wherever it may be; 
(c) any person in any place without and beyond India committing offence targeting a computer 
resource located in India. 
Explanation.—In this section, the word “offence” includes every act committed outside India which, 
if committed in India, would be punishable under this Sanhita. 
A, who is a citizen of India, commits a murder in any place without and beyond India. 
He can be tried and convicted of murder in any place in India in which he may be found. 
(6) Nothing in this Sanhita shall affect the provisions of any Act for punishing mutiny and desertion 
of officers, soldiers, sailors or airmen in the service of the Government of India or the provisions of any 
special or local law.

Now, it is proposed to enact a new law, namely, the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita Bill, 2023 by 
repealing the Indian Penal Code to streamline provisions relating to offences and penalties. It is proposed 
to provide first time community service as one of the punishments for petty offences. The offences 
against women and children, murder and offences against the State have been given precedence. The 
various offences have been made gender neutral. In order to deal effectively with the problem of 
organised crimes and terrorist activities, new offences of terrorist acts and organised crime have been 
added in the Bill with deterrent punishments. A new offence on acts of secession, armed rebellion, 
subversive activities, separatist activities or endangering sovereignty or unity and integrity of India has 
also been added. The fines and punishment for various offences have also been suitably enhanced.

Non-appearance in response to a proclamation under section 84 of Bharatiya Nagarik 
Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.—Whoever fails to appear at the specified place and the specified time as 
required by a proclamation published under sub-section (1) of section 84 of the Bharatiya Nagarik 
Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, 
or with fine, or with both, or with community service, and where a declaration has been made under 
sub-section (4) of that section pronouncing him as a proclaimed offender, he shall be punished with 
imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years and shall also be liable to fine.

Accordingly, a Bill, namely, the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 was introduced in the Lok Sabha 
on 11th August, 2023. The Bill was referred to the Department-related Parliamentary Standing 
Committee on Home Affairs for its consideration and report. The Committee after deliberations made its 
recommendations in its report submitted on 10th November, 2023. The recommendations made by the 
Committee have been considered by the Government and it has been decided to withdraw the Bill 
pending in Lok Sabha and introduce a new Bill incorporating therein those recommendations made by the 
Committee that have been accepted by the Government.

Statements conducing to public mischief.—(1) Whoever makes, publishes or circulates any 
statement, false information, rumour, or report, including through electronic means— 
(a) with intent to cause, or which is likely to cause, any officer, soldier, sailor or airman in the 
Army, Navy or Air Force of India to mutiny or otherwise disregard or fail in his duty as such; or 
(b) with intent to cause, or which is likely to cause, fear or alarm to the public, or to any section 
of the public whereby any person may be induced to commit an offence against the State or against 
the public tranquillity; or 
(c) with intent to incite, or which is likely to incite, any class or community of persons to commit 
any offence against any other class or community, 
shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both. 
(2) Whoever makes, publishes or circulates any statement or report containing false information, 
rumour or alarming news, including through electronic means, with intent to create or promote, or which 
is likely to create or promote, on grounds of religion, race, place of birth, residence, language, caste or 
community or any other ground whatsoever, feelings of enmity, hatred or ill will between different 
religious, racial, language or regional groups or castes or communities, shall be punished with 
imprisonment which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both. 
(3) Whoever commits an offence specified in sub-section (2) in any place of worship or in any 
assembly engaged in the performance of religious worship or religious ceremonies, shall be punished 
with imprisonment which may extend to five years and shall also be liable to fine. 
Exception.—It does not amount to an offence, within the meaning of this section, when the person 
making, publishing or circulating any such statement, false information, rumour or report, has reasonable 
grounds for believing that such statement, false information, rumour or report is true and makes, 
publishes or circulates it in good faith and without any such intent as aforesaid.

Imputations, assertions prejudicial to national integration.—(1) Whoever, by words either 
spoken or written or by signs or by visible representations or through electronic communication or 
otherwise,— 
(a) makes or publishes any imputation that any class of persons cannot, by reason of their being 
members of any religious, racial, language or regional group or caste or community, bear true faith 
and allegiance to the Constitution of India as by law established or uphold the sovereignty and 
integrity of India; or

(b) asserts, counsels, advises, propagates or publishes that any class of persons shall, by reason of 
their being members of any religious, racial, language or regional group or caste or community, be 
denied, or deprived of their rights as citizens of India; or 
(c) makes or publishes any assertion, counsel, plea or appeal concerning the obligation of any 
class of persons, by reason of their being members of any religious, racial, language or regional 
group or caste or community, and such assertion, counsel, plea or appeal causes or is likely to cause 
disharmony or feelings of enmity or hatred or ill-will between such members and other persons; or 
(d) makes or publishes false or misleading information, jeopardising the sovereignty, unity and 
integrity or security of India, 
shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both. 
(2) Whoever commits an offence specified in sub-section (1) in any place of worship or in any 
assembly engaged in the performance of religious worship or religious ceremonies, shall be punished 
with imprisonment which may extend to five years and shall also be liable to fine. 

CHAPTER XII 
OF OFFENCES BY OR RELATING TO PUBLIC SERVANTS

Preventing service of summons or other proceeding, or preventing publication thereof.—
Whoever in any manner intentionally prevents the serving on himself, or on any other person, of any 
summons, notice or order proceeding from any public servant legally competent, as such public servant, 
to issue such summons, notice or order, or intentionally prevents the lawful affixing to any place of any 
such summons, notice or order or intentionally removes any such summons, notice or order from any 
place to which it is lawfully affixed or intentionally prevents the lawful making of any proclamation, 
under the authority of any public servant legally competent, as such public servant, to direct such 
proclamation to be made,— 
(b) where the summons, notice, order or proclamation is to attend in person or by agent, or to 
produce a document or electronic record in a Court, with simple imprisonment for a term which may 
extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees, or with both.

Punishment for false evidence.—(1) Whoever intentionally gives false evidence in any stage 
of a judicial proceeding, or fabricates false evidence for the purpose of being used in any stage of a 
judicial proceeding, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may 
extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees. 
(2) Whoever intentionally gives or fabricates false evidence in any case other than that referred to in 
sub-section (1), shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to 
three years, and shall also be liable to fine which may extend to five thousand rupees. 
Explanation 1.—A trial before a Court-martial is a judicial proceeding. 
Explanation 2.—An investigation directed by law preliminary to a proceeding before a Court, is a 
stage of a judicial proceeding, though that investigation may not take place before a Court. 
A, in an enquiry before a Magistrate for the purpose of ascertaining whether Z ought to be committed 
for trial, makes on oath a statement which he knows to be false. As this enquiry is a stage of a judicial 
proceeding, A has given false evidence.

Explanation 3.—An investigation directed by a Court according to law, and conducted under the 
authority of a Court, is a stage of a judicial proceeding, though that investigation may not take place 
before a Court. 

A, in an enquiry before an officer deputed by a Court to ascertain on the spot the boundaries of land, 
makes on oath a statement which he knows to be false. As this enquiry is a stage of a judicial proceeding, 
A has given false evidence.
